CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS:
  S0 (244,239), S1 (465,241) - deg=3 plain T's where the two upper MOSFET drain leads meet the top rail. JUNCTION; not joining would strand each drain on a one-terminal net.
  S5 (468,440) deg=4 dot=1.6 hop=3.6 - JUDGEMENT CALL, taken as JUNCTION. I dumped the pixels (inkmap at 468,447, win 26): a perfectly plain X - the horizontal rail runs unbroken through y=439..441 and the vertical runs unbroken through x=467..469, with no solder blob, no gap, and no jog of any kind. Both readings are electrically sane, so the tie-breakers apply: (a) the ink prior for this dataset says a bare crossing is a junction, and (b) decisively, THIS drafter demonstrably draws a big semicircular hop when he means 'not connected' - he did exactly that twice on this same sheet, at S6 and S8, on the very same gate wire. Leaving S5 bare is therefore a deliberate contrast. The other reading would split n3 into {MOSFET#1 source, MOSFET#6 drain} and {MOSFET#3 source, MOSFET#5 drain}, i.e. 11 nets instead of 10.
  S6 (340,442) deg=4 hop=23.0 - CROSSING. inkmap at (338,442) shows the vertical gate wire (x~319) bulging right to x~340 across y 425..460 and returning - a textbook hop over the horizontal rail. Joining them would short MOSFET#3's gate to MOSFET#1's source node.
  S8 (344,541) deg=4 hop=31.8 - CROSSING. inkmap at (340,541) shows the same vertical wire (x~321) bulging right to x~343 across y 517..565 and returning. Joining them would short MOSFET#3's gate to the zener/gate rail n2.
  S7 (73,539) deg=3 dot=2.5 - JUNCTION. Plain T where the y~541 gate rail leaves the left column; the elevated dot score is just the corner ink. Not joining would leave the whole y~541 rail (two MOSFET gates) floating.
  S9 (192,542) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Plain T where MOSFET#1's gate lead drops onto the y~541 rail.
  S11 (465,627) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Plain T, resistor left lead onto the x~465 column.
  S12 (635,631) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Plain T, resistor right lead onto the x~635 column.
  S18 (325,664) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Plain T: the gate column runs vertically through and a branch leaves left to V-AC#10's top. Verified by zoom at (330,720): the column continues below the tee down to y~742 and then right to MOSFET#11's gate, so all three of MOSFET#3 gate / V-AC#10 top / MOSFET#11 gate are one node.
  S35 (221,801), S37 (461,805), S38 (633,805) - deg=3 plain T's onto the bottom rail. JUNCTION in every case; any of them read otherwise would strand a source or a source terminal.

MOSFET PIN ORDER (drain, gate, source) - all six had to be re-ordered, because the tracer never puts the gate at terminal index 1:
  The gate is unmistakable in every symbol: it is the long vertical plate that the odd lead leaves from, and in all six instances that lead leaves the BOTTOM end of the plate. Four devices (#1, #3, #5, #11) are drawn plate-on-the-left with the gate lead going left; two (#6, #13) are mirrored, plate-on-the-right with the gate lead going right - I confirmed #6 and #13 by 7x zoom at (690,560) and (690,740), where the three channel stubs clearly sit to the LEFT of the plate and the lone lead exits right.
  Drain vs source: the drawing does not mark it - the bulk arrow sits on the middle (body) stub, not on a terminal, and the drain and source stubs are geometrically identical. All six symbols have the same vertical orientation (gate lead off the bottom of the plate in every case, none is flipped top-to-bottom), so I used the canonical symbol layout, DRAIN = the upper lead, SOURCE = the lower lead. This also agrees with the physical reading for the NMOS devices: MOSFET#3's upper lead goes straight to the top rail that carries the 5V supply, and MOSFET#11's and #13's lower leads go straight to the bottom rail. I am recording this explicitly because it is the one thing on this sheet the ink cannot settle; if the benchmark's convention is source-up for the two P-channel devices, #1 and #6 would need t0 and t2 swapped.
  Applied: #1 (P) t0=p2 top(248,280) t1=p0 gate(196,364) t2=p1 bottom(255,381); #3 (N) t0=p1 top(467,295) t1=p0 gate(412,380) t2=p2 bottom(469,395); #5 (N) t0=p2 top(467,475) t1=p0 gate(422,544) t2=p1 bottom(466,561); #6 (P) t0=p0 top(647,470) t1=p2 gate(701,541) t2=p1 bottom(640,560); #11 (N) t0=p1 top(465,677) t1=p0 gate(414,742) t2=p2 bottom(462,759); #13 (N) t0=p1 top(636,693) t1=p0 gate(688,756) t2=p2 bottom(636,773).

CLASSES: all fourteen match the drawn symbols - I checked each MOSFET's body arrow direction, and this drafter's convention (P-channel arrow pointing toward the channel, N-channel arrow pointing away) is consistent across all six and consistent with the given labels. The zener at (69,378) has the bent 'Z' cathode bar. V-DC = circle with +/- , V-AC = circle with a sine, I-AC = circle with a sine and an arrow. Nothing looks mis-classed.
